stem: During whose reign was the Iron Pillar, which now stands at Mehrauli in Delhi, erected?
options: Chandragupta Maurya
Chandragupta II
Samudragupta
Chandragupta I
explanation: Correct option: (B). The 6-tonne pillar was erected during the reign of Chandragupta II of the Gupta dynasty. Chandragupta Maurya belonged to the earlier Maurya dynasty, Samudragupta was Chandragupta II's father and Chandragupta I was his grandfather.

stem: A bicycle left out in the rain rusts within a year, yet the Iron Pillar has stood in the open for centuries without rusting. How do scientists explain this?
options: A thin layer formed by its special iron and the air's oxygen protects it
It was painted with a thick coat of gold that has protected it ever since
It stood indoors in a temple hall for most of its long history
It is made of bronze, a mixture of copper and tin, not of iron
explanation: Correct option: (A). Scientists believe a unique thin layer, created by the special iron used and oxygen from the air, forms on the surface and protects it from corrosion. The pillar is iron, not bronze; it stands under the open sky; and no gold coating is mentioned.

stem: Historians write the name of the ruler of the Iron Pillar as 'Chandragupta II'. What does the 'II' tell us?
options: He was the second son of Samudragupta to become king
He ruled the empire twice, returning after a short exile
An earlier Gupta king, his grandfather, had the same name
He was the second Gupta ruler after the dynasty's founder
explanation: Correct option: (C). Historians added the number because an earlier Chandragupta, his grandfather Chandragupta I, ruled before him. The number says nothing about birth order, a second reign or his place in the list of rulers.

Historians identify this 'Chandra' with the Gupta king Chandragupta II

stem: Samudragupta reinstated many kings he had defeated, and they then paid him tribute. Why might this policy have suited the ruler of a vast empire?
options: Local kings kept order and paid tribute, so he need not govern every region himself
It meant he never had to fight any battle, since every king surrendered without a war
It let the reinstated kings stop paying any taxes, which kept them loyal to him for ever
It handed the Gupta throne to the strongest of the defeated kings after his own death
explanation: Correct option: (A). Reinstated kings kept running their kingdoms, paid tribute and could be asked to supply his armies, so the empire grew without direct rule everywhere. He did fight many wars, tributary kings did pay, and the Gupta throne stayed with his own family.

stem: Elsewhere in his travelogue, Faxian describes the harsh treatment of the chandalas. Why does this detail matter to a historian reading his excerpt on happy, prosperous cities?
options: It shows that his picture of a happy society did not cover everyone
It proves that his whole account is false and must be wholly set aside
It shows that everyone in the Gupta cities was treated as an equal
It shows that chandalas lived in the richest parts of the cities
explanation: Correct option: (A). The chandalas were regarded as outcastes and lived outside the city limits, so the happy picture describes only part of society. This does not make the whole account false, and it contradicts the ideas of equal treatment or chandalas living in rich areas.

stem: Read the case 'A traveller describes Gupta society'. Which conclusion would a careful historian draw from Faxian's account?

stem: Prabhavati Gupta, daughter of Chandragupta II, married a prince of the Vakataka kingdom. How did this marriage help the Guptas?
options: It brought the Pallava kingdom under direct Gupta rule

stem: Archaeologists found pottery, inscriptions in the Brahmi script and a Buddhist stupa design on Socotra Island in the Arabian Sea. What do these finds show?
options: Socotra was a province ruled directly by the Gupta kings
Socotra was the capital of an Indian kingdom of the time
Indian traders were present there over several centuries
Buddhism first began on Socotra and then spread to India
explanation: Correct option: (C). Socotra was a stop on the way to Mediterranean markets, and these finds establish the presence of Indian traders there, alongside traders from Egypt, Arabia, Rome and Greece. They do not show Gupta rule, an Indian capital there, or that Buddhism began there.

stem: Instead of controlling everything from the centre, the Guptas divided the empire into provinces and granted land to local rulers, priests and chieftains. Which is the best evaluation of this system?
options: It removed all local leaders and kept every power in the capital
It ended taxation, since the land was given away to local people
It broke the empire up, as each province soon became fully independent
It eased tax collection while letting local leaders keep some control
explanation: Correct option: (D). The system helped ensure proper tax collection and efficient government while giving local leaders some control over their regions. It did not remove local leaders, end taxes (land tax was the main revenue), or make the provinces independent.

stem: Aryabhata gave the length of a year as 365 days, 6 hours, 12 minutes and 30 seconds. The modern value is 365 days, 5 hours, 48 minutes and 45 seconds. How did his value compare?
options: About 23 minutes 45 seconds shorter
About 23 minutes 45 seconds longer
About 36 minutes 15 seconds longer
About 1 hour 24 minutes longer
explanation: Correct option: (B). Working: 6 h 12 min 30 s minus 5 h 48 min 45 s = 5 h 72 min 30 s minus 5 h 48 min 45 s = 24 min 30 s minus 45 s = 23 min 45 s. His value is the larger one, so it was 23 minutes 45 seconds longer, not shorter; the other figures come from subtraction errors.

stem: Why do some historians call the Gupta period the 'classical age' of India?
options: It was the very first period in which India was ruled by kings
Only one tradition was supported and all others were turned away
Its rulers stopped all trade so that they could focus on the arts
Long peace and stability led to great achievements in many fields
explanation: Correct option: (D). Prolonged peace strengthened the economy and let the state support scholars, artists and scientists, so literature, mathematics, astronomy, medicine and metallurgy flourished. There were many kings before the Guptas, they supported Buddhist institutions such as Nalanda too, and trade thrived.

stem: Ayurveda has roots going back several centuries BCE, yet the chapter says it was 'codified' during the Gupta period. What does this mean?
options: Older knowledge was compiled and given final shape in texts
Ayurveda was invented for the first time by Gupta court doctors
Ayurveda texts were translated from books Faxian brought
Its rules were turned into secret codes for royal doctors
explanation: Correct option: (A). Codified means arranged or written in an organised and systematic way: texts such as the Charaka Samhita and Sushruta Samhita were compiled and given their final shape then. Ayurveda was much older, did not come from Faxian's books, and 'codified' has nothing to do with secret codes.
